title: 1Password breach exposed your email and name, but your vault is safe
summary: A full root cause analysis is due in the coming weeks
content: 1Password says an attacker copied customer account records from its backend systems, including the names and email addresses people use to sign in. The company says vault contents and the keys that protect them were not affected, which leaves phishing as the main risk.

title: 6 mind-blowing Netflix genre miniseries made for a weekend binge
summary: These shows will blow your mind and not waste your time.
content: What do you do when you want to watch something that's longer than a movie, but not as long as a multi-season series that will require your undivided attention for potentially weeks on end? That's where the miniseries, or limited series, comes in. These shows are designed to be binged over a weekend, and there aren't enough of them made.
tags: The Dark Crystal: Age of Resistance

title: Claude helped me clean up my network, and it’s faster than ever
summary: Claude scanned my network, and my first problem wasn't Wi-Fi speed.
content: My home network has been quietly getting overloaded for some time now. I have my router dialed in how I want, but I haven't bothered to run Ethernet cables to my office, so most of my devices, including my main laptop, home server, Home Assistant VM, and a bunch of ESP32s are all running on inconsistent Wi-Fi signals.

title: Why closing vents in unused rooms raises your heating bill, and what to do instead
summary: My furnace had no idea I'd shut those registers, and the ductwork made me pay for it.
content: I thought that I could close the vents in my unused rooms at my old house and save some money that way. In reality, all this did was make my vent registers noisy, cause uneven heat, and prevent one of my rooms from ever heating up well. To top it all off, my energy bill increased a little bit as well.

title: Anker eufy Omni S2 Pro review: So good that my old robot vacuum is heading to the barn
summary: Day one cost me a new app, a full remap, and a standoff with four dining chairs — then it started cleaning.
content: Two eufy X10 Pro Omni robot vacuums have been keeping my house tidy for nearly a year (one on the main floor, one in the basement). They get to work as soon as I leave the house, and they're doing a decent job keeping up with my two kids and our black lab, Bella. So when Anker eufy reached out to me to try its new Omni S2 Pro , I didn't hesitate.

title: Every way to watch local news on your TV for free in 2026
summary: From over the air setups to NewsON and Local Now growth, find practical coverage that matches your market.
content: Earlier this year, I wrote about how I like to watch local news even though I cut the cord years ago . I also mentioned the best ways to do so for free. A few months later, that list already needs an update. Since then, one of the apps on my list has a new owner, while another has added over 100 new local stations. At the same time, the big networks keep pushing their own local news streams on free services.

title: Google TV has a hidden developer menu, and 3 settings in it can make a TV feel twice as fast
summary: Give your TV a speed boost
content: It's fair to say Google TVs are as slow as smartphones from the 2010s. Much of the lag comes from long animations, apps that never really close, and ads that take up more than half of your TV. People have developed apps that declutter your Google TV and make it fast and super smooth. But before you do that, you can tweak a few settings inside the hidden developer menu.

title: OpenAI admits a billing error, and your GPT-6.2 usage now burns faster
summary: OpenAI blames a launch mistake and offers one saved reset
content: OpenAI says it made a billing mistake when GPT-6.2 launched, undercounting how much usage Astra and Sol consumed. Now that the issue has been fixed, the same tasks use more of your plan's allowance, and OpenAI is adding one banked reset as an apology.

title: I checked my Android’s saved Wi-Fi list, and it was still auto-joining networks from years ago
summary: That old Wi-Fi network list is more risky than you think.
content: The Wi-Fi network list on your device is more than just a way to connect to routers. It's a portal back in time, showing you where you've been according to the networks you've connected to.

title: My Galaxy got sluggish every few weeks until I let it take care of itself
summary: End the cycle of your phone slowing down with these tweaks.
content: My Galaxy S22 Plus is getting slow despite having one of the latest versions of Android. Whether you have an old or new Samsung Galaxy, there are things you can do to make your phone feel less laggy, like having your phone automatically restart itself without you needing to think about it. Then there are a few settings you flip once (like lifting the limits your phone places on its CPU to save battery) and never touch again that can make your phone feel faster.

title: PowerShell's object pipeline makes batch files look like a relic, and it's built into Windows
summary: It's time to make this switch for your everyday jobs.
content: Most people open the Command Prompt, type a single command and close it. You can use batch files to turn this into reusable routines. However, the old way started looking dated after I used PowerShell, which is already built into Windows for the same everyday jobs.

title: I run a local LLM without Ollama, Docker, or installing anything
summary: This one file turns any computer into a local AI chatbot
content: A few weeks ago, a colleague handed me a single file from a USB stick. I double-clicked it. A chat window opened in my browser, and I started talking to an LLM. No Ollama, Docker, or LM Studio.

title: Windows' best free screenshot app just got much better at copying text off your screen
summary: The update is out as a pre-release for now
content: ShareX 22.5.0 replaces Windows' built-in OCR with a local AI engine that can recognize text in over 100 languages . There's no language pack to install or language to pick. The project says the results are significantly more accurate , and the update is currently available as a pre-release .

title: The 12 best deep search engines to explore the invisible web
summary: Most of the internet is hidden from your view unless you know how to search for it.
content: Not everything on the web will show up in Google or Bing search results; many places are inaccessible to search engine crawlers.

title: This free tool brings your Windows-only USB gear to Linux
summary: Record app traffic, map settings to USB messages, and get a Python driver plus a report showing how choices were found.
content: Thanks to USB-REA , a free, open-source tool, you can generate a Linux driver for pretty much any USB gadget that comes with a Windows-only app. It works by analyzing the messages that the app sends to your device and writing a Python driver that can send commands of its own.

title: This new LCD backlight promises to outshine and outlast OLED
summary: Tiny RGB LEDs placed directly behind an LCD panel claim cinema-standard colors and blistering peak brightness.
content: Seoul Semiconductor has started producing a new RGB backlight for LCD TVs and supplying it to TV makers around the world. According to its November 25 announcement , the technology, called WICOP Pixel, can reach a peak brightness of 3,000 nits and last twice as long as a regular OLED screen.

title: Zelda and Mario 64 now run natively on PC, and emulation has nothing to do with it
summary: Emulation is no longer the future.
content: Emulation might just be on its way out, and decompilation is why. We’ve seen a ton of AI-assisted homebrew and game decompilation projects emerge at the end of 2026, all with the singular goal of achieving a fully compatible PC port.
